name: AI
title:
Assessing AI
robustness
summary: A research prototype for evaluating LLM attacks and verifying LoRA adapters, with measurements and defined limitations.

chapters.label: PROBLEM
chapters.title:
Model behavior
needs verification
chapters.text: Adversarial inputs can change language-model behavior. Third-party LoRA adapters also require verification. Before adopting a defense, both robustness and its effect on answer quality need evaluation.

chapters.label: SOLUTION
chapters.title:
Test the defense
in a controlled setting
chapters.text: The prototype combines session-based LoRA parameter shifts, attack simulation and computation auditing. It supports experimental comparison of model behavior and answer quality under different defense settings.

chapters.label: HOW IT WORKS
chapters.title:
Assess protection
and answer quality
chapters.text: The testbed simulates attacks and compares model behavior under different defense settings. A separate auditor verifies computations against a reference model. Evaluation covers both robustness and the cost of protection: changes in answers and computational overhead.

details.title: Implementation details
details.text: The prototype derives a verifiable shift using Ed25519 and SHAKE-256. The inference server and auditor can run in separate processes: the auditor reproduces the shift on a reference model and compares logits. The protection module is registered as software under No. 2025665020.

chapters.label: OUTCOME
chapters.title:
A basis for pilots,
with measured limits
chapters.text: On 10 AdvBench prompts with TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, transferred GCG suffixes and direct optimization with the shift produced 0 successful attacks. Long-answer diversity also decreased. These findings support further pilot evaluations, not a claim of universal LLM protection.

details.title: Conditions and limitations
details.text: Success was defined by a target affirmative phrase at the beginning of the response. Sample: 10 AdvBench prompts; LoRA r=8; shift amplitude 0.1. On 8 MT-Bench questions, long-answer diversity decreased (distinct-2: 0.91 → 0.62), so amplitude requires tuning. Auditor verification averaged 0.772 s on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, Apple MPS, across 10 control queries. These findings apply to the described testbed and do not establish universal protection against prompt injection. The approach requires access to model weights and the LoRA adapter. The dissertation recommends standardized ECVRF for industrial use instead of the experimental scheme. Small logit perturbations may remain undetected at the chosen threshold. Natural-language prompt injections require additional detection mechanisms and restrictions on agent permissions.
